key_insight: ARMOR++ uses an agentic, multi-domain primitive set to craft transferable adversarial attacks that remain effective against deepfake detectors even in strict black-box, no-query settings. The core idea is to combine semantic awareness with coordinated attack generation so perturbations transfer better from surrogate models to modern transformer-based targets.
problem_solved: It addresses the drop in deepfake detector reliability under black-box adversarial transfer, especially when attacks must work without queries and across different model families. Existing transfer attacks often depend on architecture-specific cues and fail to generalize well from CNN surrogates to transformer-based detectors.
method: Introduces ARMOR++, a multi-agent framework that orchestrates multiple attack primitives across different domains.
Uses semantic-aware attack generation to better preserve transferability under no-query constraints.
Coordinates surrogate-crafted perturbations to improve effectiveness on target deepfake detectors, including transformer-based models.
impact: This matters because it highlights a stronger threat model for deepfake detection systems and shows that current defenses may be more fragile than expected. For practitioners, it emphasizes the need to evaluate detectors against transferable, black-box attacks rather than only white-box or query-based settings.

paper_title: ARMOR++: Agentic Orchestration of a Multi-Domain Primitive Set for Transferable Attacks on Deepfake Detectors
paper_authors: Christos Korgialas, Gabriel Lee Jun Rong, Dion Jia Xu Ho, Pai Chet Ng, Xiaoxiao Miao
